title: The accuracy statistics recomputed in base R over frozen residual vectors
question: Does checkpointAccuracy compute bias, RMSE and the maximum absolute residual, and does the NVA figure derived as 1.96 times that RMSE, agree with an independent base-R recomputation over six frozen residual vectors, and with the closed forms four of them carry?

claims.toleranceDerivation: Both sides read the same exact decimal literals and both accumulate in double, so the only arithmetic difference left is summation order over at most a hundred terms, which is bounded by a few multiples of 2.2e-16 on quantities of order 1 to 100. 1e-12 sits several orders above that floor and far below any vertical accuracy figure a reader would act on, so a difference above it would be a formula difference and not round-off. The tolerance is never widened to reach agreement.

freeze.witness: The commit that added the residual fixtures, the R script and tests/statisticsRAgreement.test.ts, where the 1e-12 tolerance appears as the constant TOL. The tolerance and the reference output arrive together in that commit, so no commit shows the tolerance while the comparison had no result.

decisionRule: The study reports agreement only on the quantities that carry no order statistic: bias, RMSE, the maximum absolute residual, and the NVA figure derived from RMSE. Median, NMAD and P95 depend on a quantile convention, R interpolates at type 7 and checkpointAccuracy takes the nearest rank, and the difference is recorded rather than counted as agreement or as error. Where a closed form exists it is scored first, because two programs computing the same wrong statistic agree perfectly.
notes: Base R only, so the reference depends on nothing beyond the R build recorded here.

The study found two quantile conventions inside this repository: src/terrain/quantile.ts interpolates and src/validation/checkpointAccuracy.ts takes the nearest rank. Reconciling them is a change to a validation module and is outside this protocol.
